part.text:
I have all the information needed. No files were modified. Here is my final answer.

## Answer

**Yes.** curl can print transfer stats as JSON with `-w/--write-out` using `-w "%{json}"`.

## Supporting commit

The commit that establishes this is:

**`04c03416e68fd635a15cae8201872f5c29fdcca8`** — "writeout: support to generate JSON output"
- Author: Mathias Gumz `<mg@2hoch5.com>` (Feb 1, 2020)
- Committed by Daniel Stenberg on **Tue Mar 17 15:01:28 2020**
- Closes [#4870](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/4870)
- Confirmed to be an ancestor of the pinned HEAD (`ee521a1c8`), and the feature exists in the current checkout (`docs/cmdline-opts/write-out.d` documents the `json` variable; `src/tool_writeout_json.c` exists).

### Quote from the commit message

> ```
> writeout: support to generate JSON output
>
> This commit adds support to generate JSON via the writeout feature:
>
>     -w "%{json}"
>
> It leverages the existing infrastructure as much as possible. Thus,
> generating the JSON on STDERR is possible by:
>
>     -w "%{stderr}%{json}"
>
> This implements a variant of
> https://github.com/curl/curl/wiki/JSON#--write-out-json.
>
> Closes #4870
> ```

### Quote from the diff

`docs/cmdline-opts/write-out.d` gained a new documented variable:

> ```
> +.B json
> +A JSON object with all available keys.
> ```

The commit also added `src/tool_writeout_json.c` (181 lines) and `src/tool_writeout_json.h`, wired the new variable into `src/tool_writeout.c`, and bumped `lib/version.c`.

### Subsequent history (for context)

The `%{json}` output was refined by later ancestors of HEAD such as `ab9dc5ae2` ("writeout_json: add missing comma to fix the HTTP version"), `8d9802b0a`, `884de1a76`, `2f78be51e`, `65ca22946`, and `7631f2b75` ("test 970: verify --write-out '%{json}'"). A related `%{header_json}` variable was added later in `4133a69f2`.

So your memory is correct: `-w "%{json}"` exists (introduced in curl 7.70.0, per the March 2020 commit date).
